heroHeadline: Day 608: CNTE National Strike Megamarch Shuts Down Mexico City on Week Before World Cup; Sheinbaum Announces Tomato Price Deal for June 3; Informe Reactions Cite 'We Are Not Anyone's Puppet'
heroSubtitle: June 1, 2026 marks Day 608 of Claudia Sheinbaum's presidency. The CNTE executed its announced national work stoppage, with a megamarch of tens of thousands of teachers departing the Ángel de la Independencia on Paseo de la Reforma toward the Zócalo and Centro Histórico, shutting down major arteries including Reforma, Juárez, Eje Central, and 5 de Mayo. The strike affected 29 states — led by Sección 22 (Oaxaca, ~70,000), Sección 7 (Chiapas), Sección 18 (Michoacán) — with the Zócalo partially blocked by FIFA World Cup Fan Fest infrastructure ahead of the June 11 Mexico vs. South Africa opener. Core demands (ISSSTE pension abrogation, 100% salary raise, end of teacher evaluation system) remain unmet after three SEGOB dialogue rounds. At her Day 608 mañanera, Sheinbaum announced a June 3 tomato price-relief agreement with producers and distributors (citing Florida frosts + Sinaloa disease + intermediary markups), presented four young women to represent Mexico at the World Cup inauguration ceremony, confirmed 18.8M bienestar payments June 15–21 (663M pesos), and extended her sovereignty posture in response to U.S. DOJ indictment pressure: 'We are not anyone's puppet — if from abroad culprits are dictated, that is interference.' Reactions to the May 31 Second Government Report continued across international media, with Al Jazeera and Vallarta Daily publishing June 1 analysis of Sheinbaum's 'hardened' U.S. message at the Monumento a la Revolución rally.
